title: Divided powers on the split square-zero extension of a divided-power ideal
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset C$ an ideal with an ordinary divided-power structure $\gamma$ [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure], and $M$ a $C$-module. Give $B=C\oplus M$ multiplication $(c,u)(d,v)=(cd,cv+du)$ and unit $(1,0)$, and put $K=I\oplus M\subset B$. There is a unique ordinary divided-power structure $\delta$ on $K$ such that $\delta_n(x,0)=(\gamma_n(x),0)$ for $x\in I$ and $\delta_n(0,u)=0$ for $u\in M$, $n>1$. For $n\geq1$ it is given by $\delta_n(x,u)=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)u)$. Here an ordinary divided-power structure $\eta$ on an ideal $L$ of a commutative ring $D$ means maps $\eta_n:L\to L$ for $n\geq1$, with $\eta_0(z)=1$, satisfying $\eta_1(z)=z$, $\eta_n(dz)=d^n\eta_n(z)$, $\eta_n(z+w)=\sum_{i=0}^n\eta_i(z)\eta_{n-i}(w)$, $\eta_n(z)\eta_m(z)=\binom{n+m}{n}\eta_{n+m}(z)$ and $\eta_n(\eta_m(z))=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}\eta_{nm}(z)$ for $d\in D$, $z,w\in L$, and $n,m\geq1$. The factorial quotients are integer coefficients, not divisions in $D$.

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), ordinary even-part calculation underlying the displayed formula; expanded split square-zero argument using the axioms of Tag 07GP (lemma-check-on-generators).

proof.text: Use the five axioms of [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure]. The stated multiplication is associative: the second component of either triple product is $cdw+cev+deu$ for factors $(c,u),(d,v),(e,w)$; commutativity and the unit follow immediately. Moreover $K=I\oplus M$ is an ideal since $cx\in I$. Define $\delta_0(z)=(1,0)$ and, for $n\geq1$, $\delta_n(x,u)=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)u)$. Its first component lies in $I$, so it maps $K$ into $K$. We have $\delta_1(x,u)=(x,u)$.

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), displayed extension formula; Tag 07GL (definition-divided-powers), axioms (1)-(5).

proof.text: Two elementary consequences of the cited ordinary axioms will be used explicitly. For every $r\geq1$, scalar compatibility with scalar zero gives $\gamma_r(0)=0$. Also $x\gamma_{r-1}(x)=r\gamma_r(x)$: for $r=1$ this is $x\cdot1=x$, and for $r>1$ it is the product axiom with indices $1,r-1$. Thus the constructed operations restrict to $(\gamma_n(x),0)$ on $(x,0)$, and $\delta_n(0,u)=0$ for $n>1$, while $\delta_1(0,u)=(0,u)$.

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), displayed extension formula; Tag 07GL (definition-divided-powers), axioms (1)-(5).

proof.text: Check the scalar axiom for every scalar $b=(c,v)\in B$, not just for $c\in C$. For $n=1$ it is immediate. For $n\geq2$, induction using the multiplication in $B$ gives $b^n=(c^n,nc^{n-1}v)$. For $z=(x,u)$, the first components of $\delta_n(bz)$ and $b^n\delta_n(z)$ are $c^n\gamma_n(x)$. Their second components are respectively $c^n\gamma_{n-1}(x)u+c^{n-1}x\gamma_{n-1}(x)v$ and $c^n\gamma_{n-1}(x)u+nc^{n-1}\gamma_n(x)v$; these agree by $x\gamma_{n-1}(x)=n\gamma_n(x)$, established in step 2. No cancellation in $C$ or $M$ is used.

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), displayed extension formula; Tag 07GL (definition-divided-powers), axioms (1)-(5).

proof.text: Check addition for $z=(x,u)$ and $w=(y,v)$ in $K$. At $n=0$ both sides are $(1,0)$. For $n\geq1$, the first component of $\sum_{i=0}^n\delta_i(z)\delta_{n-i}(w)$ is $\sum_{i=0}^n\gamma_i(x)\gamma_{n-i}(y)=\gamma_n(x+y)$. The coefficient of $u$ in its second component is $\sum_{i=1}^n\gamma_{i-1}(x)\gamma_{n-i}(y)=\gamma_{n-1}(x+y)$, and the coefficient of $v$ is $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\gamma_i(x)\gamma_{n-i-1}(y)=\gamma_{n-1}(x+y)$. These are precisely the two components of $\delta_n(z+w)$, by the addition axiom for $\gamma$ (including its tautological degree-zero case).

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), displayed extension formula; Tag 07GL (definition-divided-powers), axioms (1)-(5).

proof.text: For positive $n,m$, the first component of $\delta_n(z)\delta_m(z)$ is $\binom{n+m}{n}\gamma_{n+m}(x)$. The second is $(\gamma_n(x)\gamma_{m-1}(x)+\gamma_{n-1}(x)\gamma_m(x))u$. Apply the product axiom for $\gamma$, using $\gamma_0=1$ when an index is zero, to rewrite it as $\bigl(\binom{n+m-1}{n}+\binom{n+m-1}{n-1}\bigr)\gamma_{n+m-1}(x)u$. Pascal's identity makes this $\binom{n+m}{n}\gamma_{n+m-1}(x)u$, as required for the product axiom for $\delta$. Pascal's identity here is the integer identity obtained by classifying $n$-element subsets according to whether they contain a fixed element.

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), displayed extension formula; Tag 07GL (definition-divided-powers), axioms (1)-(5).

proof.text: Write $q(a,b)=(ab)!/(a!(b!)^a)$ for the integer coefficient in the iteration axiom, with positive $a,b$. Iteration with outer index $n=1$ is immediate. For $n\geq2$ and $m\geq1$, the first component of $\delta_n(\delta_m(x,u))$ is $q(n,m)\gamma_{nm}(x)$. Its second is $\gamma_{n-1}(\gamma_m(x))\gamma_{m-1}(x)u=q(n-1,m)\gamma_{(n-1)m}(x)\gamma_{m-1}(x)u$. The product axiom, with its degree-zero case if $m=1$, makes this $q(n-1,m)\binom{nm-1}{m-1}\gamma_{nm-1}(x)u$. The integer coefficient equals $q(n,m)$: multiplying the factorial expressions gives $\frac{(nm-1)!}{(n-1)!(m!)^{n-1}(m-1)!}=\frac{(nm)!}{n!(m!)^n}$. This equality is verified in $\mathbf Q$ between integers before mapping them into $C$; it does not divide by any element of $C$. This proves the iteration axiom and completes all five axioms for $\delta$.

source.place: Tag 09PH (example-adjoining-odd), displayed extension formula; Tag 07GL (definition-divided-powers), axioms (1)-(5).

proof.text: For uniqueness let $\eta$ be any ordinary structure with the required restrictions. Its degree-one map is the identity. For $n\geq2$ apply its addition axiom to $(x,u)=(x,0)+(0,u)$. Since $\eta_j(0,u)=0$ for $j>1$, only the terms with $j=0,1$ survive, yielding $\eta_n(x,u)=(\gamma_n(x),0)+(\gamma_{n-1}(x),0)(0,u)=(\gamma_n(x),\gamma_{n-1}(x)u)$. The zeroth map is fixed by convention. Thus every operation agrees with the constructed one, proving uniqueness.

lean.statement: theorem exists_unique (C : Type u) [CommRing C] (I : Ideal C) (γ : DividedPowers I) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module C M] : ∃ δ : DividedPowers (I.comap (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom C C M).toRingHom), (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : C), x ∈ I → δ.dpow n (TrivSqZeroExt.inl x) = TrivSqZeroExt.inl (γ.dpow n x)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (u : M), 1 < n → δ.dpow n (TrivSqZeroExt.inr u) = 0) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : C) (u : M), 0 < n → x ∈ I → δ.dpow n (TrivSqZeroExt.inl x + TrivSqZeroExt.inr u) = TrivSqZeroExt.inl (γ.dpow n x) + TrivSqZeroExt.inr (γ.dpow (n - 1) x • u)) ∧ ∀ η : DividedPowers (I.comap (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom C C M).toRingHom), (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : C), x ∈ I → η.dpow n (TrivSqZeroExt.inl x) = TrivSqZeroExt.inl (γ.dpow n x)) → (∀ (n : ℕ) (u : M), 1 < n → η.dpow n (TrivSqZeroExt.inr u) = 0) → η = δ
